title: Tanh logit softcap 15 on the output readout (Gemma 2 / modded-nanogpt), persisting into RL, on the 081 Polar Express Muon incumbent
description: P49-adjacent (logit-scale family, but architectural rather than a pretraining-only penalty): wrap the untied readout in logits = 15*tanh(logits/15) via a forward hook on model.head, so pretraining, the frozen RL fine-tune, sampling and eval all see capped logits; no new parameters, everything else exactly as 081-claude. A smooth cap on logit magnitude stops the Muon-trained readout from pushing already-correct tokens to extreme margins on <=6-line data, which should leave a less saturated, better-conditioned policy for expert iteration to adapt to >=7-line targets.
hypothesis: With cross-entropy on mostly near-deterministic proof tokens (train loss ~0.06), the readout keeps growing logit margins after the argmax is already right; under Muon with 10x decay this spends update budget on margin inflation and yields a sharply peaked handoff policy. A tanh cap at 15 saturates the gradient for |logit| >~ 15, so learning is redirected to still-wrong tokens (the modded-nanogpt effect), and the capped function persists into RL, where the frozen AdamW fine-tune cannot re-saturate the policy either; both should raise round-1 targets solved on >=7-line targets and final RL-solved. Countervailing: if logits rarely exceed ~10 the cap is near a no-op (delta ~0); if they are large, compression of confident tokens could slow RL fitting of new proofs.
expected_delta: -40 to +40 theorems at >=7 (central -5); 404 is probably an upward draw (082-090 all 324-371)

arch.change: CHANGED versus 081-claude: output logits pass through SOFTCAP*tanh(logits/SOFTCAP), SOFTCAP=15.0, via model.head.register_forward_hook (applied in pretraining loss, harness RL fine-tune, sampling and eval; hook returns in the head's dtype). No new parameters; otherwise 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads, d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork loads the state dict unchanged, but the softcap hook is not in the state dict: an offline reload must re-register head hook 15*tanh(x/15) to reproduce the policy
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code
arch.local_check: CPU, pinned fork model.py: with head weights scaled x2000 raw logits reached 2087 and hooked logits max 15.0; n_params 4,000,000 unchanged

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 070-claude (same as 069-claude): fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude.
